newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH HOME ORDERS IN HAND HIT RECORD IN Q2.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH HOME ORDERS IN HAND HIT RECORD IN Q2.

text.p: New home commissions at architects in the Netherlands rose by seven percent to 2.17 billion guilders in the 1996 second quarter, giving a record 15.6 billion guilders of home orders in hand, the Central Bureau of Statistics said.
This was more than offset by a fall in new office commissions which fell nine percent in the same period.

The total of new orders (homes and offices) was therefore slightly lower than the year-ago period and total orders in hand also dropped by 0.5 billion guilders to 33.4 billion from the first quarter record of 33.9 billion.
The number of new homes commissioned was lower than last year, but their average value was much higher, the CBS said.
Order intake at architects runs approximately five quarters ahead of the start of construction and is an important indicator for building activities.
